questions.q: Read «يَلْهَث ذَّٰلِكَ» (7:176) and «وَقُل رَّبِّ» (17:24): name the meeting and how to read it.
questions.a: ث into ذ: mutajanisayn, yalhadh-dhaalik. ل into ر: mutaqaribayn, wa qur-rabbi.

questions.q: Meeting-letters sort (pupil PDF): sort 9 examples into mithlayn, mutajanisayn, mutaqaribayn. Today's rota group recites 69:1 to 12.
questions.a: Mithlayn: ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ, عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ, رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمْ. Mutajanisayn: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ, قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ, إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓا۟. Mutaqaribayn: وَقُل رَّبِّ, نَخْلُقكُّم, and laam of al- before sun letters.

questions.q: Extend: find one mithlayn in Al-Mulk or Al-Qalam.
questions.a: Pupil gives an example (e.g. meem into meem) checked by the teacher.

questions.q: Stretch: why does the laam of al- merge into sun letters?
questions.a: Laam and the sun letters are close in makhraj (mutaqaribayn), so it merges.
A) Mutajanisayn: same makhraj. ت and ط share a makhraj but differ in sifat, so mutajanisayn; the ت merges into ط.

questions.q: Think again: When two people with the same name meet, how do we keep them apart? What happens when two identical letters meet?
questions.a: Identical letters usually merge into one with a shaddah (mithlayn): ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ.
